  PROBLEM: §21.F step 1 runs `git checkout -b <branch>-resend` before checking whether the name is free. If the local branch already exists, the checkout fails before suffix selection. If it does not exist, the checkout creates it, so the later local `git rev-parse` check always reports it taken and the session advances to `-resend-2`.
  WHY: The availability check is ordered after the action it is meant to gate, so the `-resend-N` escalation is unreachable as written. Reviewers rated this MAJOR, mapped here to high. Only some reviewers described the always-taken case.

- .claude/docs/s21-merged-pr-commit-guard.md:232-237 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5

  WHY: A long-lived session hitting the fallback repeatedly is the case §21.F was written for, and it is the case that breaks.

  WHY: A leftover local `-resend` branch leaves the session stuck after the refused push. Otherwise the instructions treat the newly created default branch as occupied.

  PROBLEM: Step 1 runs `git checkout -b <branch>-resend` and only afterwards checks the name on the remote and locally. If the local branch already exists, the checkout fails before any check runs. Otherwise the local `git rev-parse` check always finds the name taken, so the session always advances to `-resend-2` and later attempts self-collide.
  WHY: Followed verbatim, a session either aborts at step 1 or keeps skipping to higher `-resend-N` suffixes, so the "use the first free one" logic is unreachable as written.
